title: Continuity of flat proper-support coherent families
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $f:X\to B$ be a finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For an $S$-scheme $T$, let $\mathcal C(T)$ be the groupoid of pairs $(b:T\to B,M)$, where $M$ is a finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{X\times_BT}$-module, flat over $T$, with support proper over $T$. Here finite presentation means etale locally a cokernel of a map between finite rank free modules; flatness is stalkwise flatness over base local rings on etale charts [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]; proper support means $M\simeq i_*N$ for a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X\times_BT$ with $Z\to T$ proper and $N$ finite type quasi-coherent [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. Modules and tensor pullback use [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module, def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Arrows over $v:T\to T_1$ are isomorphisms $v_X^*M_1\simeq M$ with $b=b_1v$; composition uses canonical pullback composition isomorphisms. Assume $B\to S$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. For every small nonempty directed inverse system $(T_i)$ of affine $S$-schemes with affine transition maps and limit $T$, the natural functor $2\operatorname{colim}_i\mathcal C(T_i)\to\mathcal C(T)$ is an equivalence. Explicitly, objects descend to a stage, isomorphisms between descended objects descend to a common later stage, and equality of stage isomorphisms after restriction to $T$ holds at some later stage. The groupoid 2-colimit uses these eventual arrows.

proof.text: First the stated restriction functor exists. For any base map $v:T'\to T$, apply [lem-sfb-space-module-base-change-flat-proper-support] to $X_T\to T$ and $M$. This morphism is locally of finite type because it is finitely presented, by base-change preservation in [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. Thus $v_X^*M$ is again quasi-coherent, finitely presented, flat over $T'$, and carried by a proper closed subspace over $T'$. Pulling back an isomorphism and its inverse gives inverse maps. Use the canonical tensor composition comparisons of [def-sfb-space-module-tensor-composition] for all iterated pullbacks; their local formula sends $c\otimes(d\otimes m)$ to $c\,v^\sharp(d)\otimes m$, so the two triple-composition maps agree by multiplication associativity. Identity comparisons have the same normalization. Hence restriction defines the comparison on the groupoid of eventual arrows.

Every $T_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Apply [lem-sfb-lfp-space-scheme-limit-test] to $Z=B$. Its sole finiteness hypothesis on the target is precisely the assumed local finite presentation of $B\to S$. Consequently every $b:T\to B$ comes from some $b_{i_0}:T_{i_0}\to B$. On the tail $i\ge i_0$ set $b_i=b_{i_0}\circ(T_i\to T_{i_0})$. Moreover any two stage base maps with equal restriction to $T$ agree after passing to a common later index, by the equality clause of the same cited statement. Restricting to a tail loses no eventual object or arrow: directedness gives an upper bound for $i_0$ and any given finite collection of indices.

Fix such a tail and put $X_i=X\times_B T_i$ and $X_T=X\times_B T$. By [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], each $f_i:X_i\to T_i$ is finitely presented, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Since $T_i$ is affine, quasi-compactness of $X_i$ is the identity affine test in the definition of quasi-compactness of $f_i$. Its quasi-separatedness follows from [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products], applied to $f_i$ and the quasi-separated $T_i$; affines are quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Each transition $X_j\to X_i$ is the base change of the affine $T_j\to T_i$, hence affine by [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality]. Apply the base-change formula of [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages] to the system $(T_i)$ and $W=X_{i_0}\to T_{i_0}$: its result is $X_T\simeq\varprojlim_{i\ge i_0}X_i$. The fibre-product identifications here follow from their universal property. For applications below to statements formulated over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] lets us forget $S$, preserving these fibre products and the small etale ringed sites. The chart definitions of finite presentation, flatness, and proper carriers then give exactly the same conditions on these objects.

Let $(b,M)$ be an object over $T$ and use steps 2 and 3 for its base map. Apply the object clause of [lem-sfb-space-fp-module-limit-category] to the small directed system $(X_i)_{i\ge i_0}$, whose affine transitions and quasi-compact quasi-separated stages were checked in step 3. Obtain an index $i\ge i_0$, a finitely presented module $M_i$ on $X_i$, and an isomorphism $M_i|_{X_T}\simeq M$. This descended module is quasi-coherent: its finite local presentation is an instance of the local free presentation defining quasi-coherence in [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Its later tensor pullbacks are still finitely presented by the preservation clause of the same module-continuity node, and are quasi-coherent for the same reason.

The limit pullback of $M_i$ is flat over $T$ in the chart sense of the item. By [lem-sfb-space-module-flat-chart-test], (ii) implies (i), this is the same as flatness of every geometric stalk over the geometric local ring of $T$, which is the flatness convention of [lem-sfb-space-module-eventually-flat]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-module-eventually-flat] to $X_i\to T_i$ and $M_i$: both are finitely presented and the base system consists of affines, exactly its hypotheses. Replace $i$ by the resulting later index, where all later pullbacks have flat geometric stalks over $T_k$; by the chart test again, (i) implies (ii) for any atlas, and any etale scheme chart together with an atlas is again an atlas, so they are flat over $T_k$ in the chart sense of the item. By [lem-sfb-space-module-proper-carrier-support], the proper carrier of $M$ makes its scheme-theoretic support proper over $T$; finite presentation implies finite type, and $X_T\to T$ is locally of finite type. Now apply [lem-sfb-space-module-eventually-proper-support] on this tail to obtain a later $j$ with proper scheme-theoretic support for $M_j$. Apply the carrier equivalence again to $X_j\to T_j$ and $M_j$ to obtain a proper closed carrier and a finite type quasi-coherent module on it. Thus $(b_j,M_j)$ is in $\mathcal C(T_j)$ and its pullback is $(b,M)$. This proves essential surjectivity. No assertion that annihilator ideals commute with arbitrary base change is used.

Take two stage objects and an isomorphism between their restrictions to $T$. Move both to a common stage. Their base maps become equal at some later stage by [lem-sfb-lfp-space-scheme-limit-test], since the limit isomorphism includes equality of base maps. We now have two finitely presented modules $F_i,G_i$ on the same $X_i$, whose limit isomorphism is $\alpha:F\to G$. Apply the morphism clause of [lem-sfb-space-fp-module-limit-category] separately to $\alpha$ and $\alpha^{-1}$, and move their descents $a,b$ to a common later stage. Their composites $ba$ and $ab$ restrict to the respective identities. Apply the equality clause of that same node to these two pairs of maps, and choose a common upper bound of the resulting indices. There $ba=1$ and $ab=1$, so $a$ is a stage isomorphism descending $\alpha$. Throughout these passages the two modules remain objects of $\mathcal C$ by step 1. Thus every arrow between two limit restrictions comes from an eventual arrow.

Suppose two eventual isomorphisms have equal restriction to $T$. Choose representatives at a common stage, and then make their base maps equal by [lem-sfb-lfp-space-scheme-limit-test]. Their module maps have the same domain and codomain after the canonical pullback comparisons. The equality clause of [lem-sfb-space-fp-module-limit-category] makes these maps equal at some later stage. They therefore represent the same eventual arrow, proving faithfulness. Conversely equality at a stage stays equality after restriction because pullback is a functor. Together with step 6 this is full faithfulness, and step 5 gives essential surjectivity, so the stated comparison is an equivalence of groupoids.

I checked it against quot.tex Situation 08KB and Lemma 08KD (lines 880-1134) and found that the statement matches, with the support hypothesis written in carrier form, equivalent by 0CZI. The report says the source writes X_T = colim X_i at line 1119 where it should be lim; that is correct. Steps 1-4, 6 and 7 are fine: every cited statement says what the step takes from it, and the hypotheses check out. These were checked: finite presentation under base change; the T_i and X_i are qcqs, the latter by the qs-over-qs clause; transitions are affine; the limit formula from affine-limits-schematic-stages; change of base to Spec Z; the object, map and equality clauses of fp-module-limit-category; and the inverse of the descended isomorphism also descends. One fault (C1/E6) is in step 5. lem-sfb-space-module-eventually-flat defines flatness by geometric stalks over geometric local rings, but the item uses Zariski stalks on etale charts. The step passed from one sense to the other silently, in both directions. The existing node lem-sfb-space-module-flat-chart-test, in the same unit and on the base, proves exactly this equivalence for any atlas. My fix cites it before and after the eventual-flatness step and adds it to uses and proof_deps. Proper support goes from carrier form to scheme-theoretic support and back through proper-carrier-support, with the hypotheses (locally finite type, finite type module) checked. Edge cases checked: one-element system, empty X_T or zero module, non-Noetherian bases, B not quasi-separated. Batch-5 check: all 12 listed citations, and the added one, reach sec-trace-formula only through the general definition def-trf-algebraic-space. They are general facts about algebraic spaces, not steps in the proof of the trace formula or Poincare duality, so I accept them. No tool_uses: affine-scheme-qcqs is a Mathlib leaf. lean.statement: theorem limit_preserving (f : X ⟶ B) (_hf : ProperQuotFinitePresentation f) (_hB : ∀ U : B.EtaleSite, LocallyOfFinitePresentation U.obj.left.hom) {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Over S) (_haff : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, IsAffine (D.obj i).left) (_htrans : ∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map a).left) (c : Cone D) (_hc : IsLimit c) : (∀ x : Fiber f c.pt, ∃ (i : I) (xi : Fiber f (D.obj (op i))), Nonempty (Lift (c.π.app (op i)) x xi)) ∧ (∀ (i : I) (xi yi : Fiber f (D.obj (op i))) (x y : Fiber f c.pt) (px : Lift (c.π.app (op i)) x xi) (py : Lift (c.π.app (op i)) y yi) (a : x ⟶ y), ∃ (j : I) (hij : i ≤ j) (xj yj : Fiber f (D.obj (op j))) (qx : Lift (D.map (homOfLE hij).op) xj xi) (qy : Lift (D.map (homOfLE hij).op) yj yi) (rx : Lift (c.π.app (op j)) x xj) (ry : Lift (c.π.app (op j)) y yj) (b : xj ⟶ yj), rx.val ≫ qx.val = px.val ∧ ry.val ≫ qy.val = py.val ∧ a.val ≫ ry.val = rx.val ≫ b.val) ∧ (∀ (i : I) (xi yi : Fiber f (D.obj (op i))) (a b : xi ⟶ yi) (x : Fiber f c.pt) (px : Lift (c.π.app (op i)) x xi), px.val ≫ a.val = px.val ≫ b.val → ∃ (j : I) (hij : i ≤ j) (xj : Fiber f (D.obj (op j))) (qx : Lift (D.map (homOfLE hij).op) xj xi), qx.val ≫ a.val = qx.val ≫ b.val)
